candidates.text: _validatePrice() must protect the buyback mechanism from price manipulation by comparing the current spot price against a time-weighted average price derived from two snapshots taken at different points in time.
evidence_ids: The _validatePrice()_ function in __UniswapPriceOracle__ is supposed to protect the protocol's buyback mechanism from price manipulation by comparing the current spot price against a time-weighted average price. Due to a mathematical error in how the TWAP is computed, the function always compares the spot price against itself, resulting in a derivation of zero every single time. The function therefore always returns true, no matter how severely the pool has been manipulated.

The fundamental problem is that the function reads _cumulativePriceLast_ from the pool and then immediately uses it as both the starting point and the reference for subtraction in the same calculation. A correct TWAP implementation needs two snapshots taken at different points in time — you need to store a previous cumulative price reading and compare it against the current one.
Add state to the oracle to store the cumulative price at a previous point in time. On each call, compare the current cumulative price against the stored one to derive a real TWAP:

candidates.text: The V2 buyback path must retain an effective pre-swap price validation so that a manipulated spot price is rejected before the swap executes.
evidence_ids: The _validatePrice()_ function in __UniswapPriceOracle__ is supposed to protect the protocol's buyback mechanism from price manipulation by comparing the current spot price against a time-weighted average price. Due to a mathematical error in how the TWAP is computed, the function always compares the spot price against itself, resulting in a derivation of zero every single time. The function therefore always returns true, no matter how severely the pool has been manipulated.
